newsitem.title: ZAIRE: Mobutu leaves Zaire, many doubt he will return.
newsitem.headline: Mobutu leaves Zaire, many doubt he will return.

text.p: President Mobutu Sese Seko flew out of Zaire on Wednesday to attend a regional summit meeting in Gabon, beginning what many residents of the capital thought might be a flight into exile.

A Reuters correspondent saw his plane depart for Libreville at 1015 local time (0915 GMT). Mobutu aides have said the president would return on Friday but there was speculation in the capital Kinshasa he would not return due to rebel advances.
There was intense security around the airport -- a declared target of the rebels -- and Mobutu left on his plane only about 10 minutes after his heavily guarded motorcade arrived.

Combat-ready troops were backed by armoured personnel carriers, heavy guns and anti-aircraft weapons to protect him as he entered the VIP lounge. Hundreds of other troops were seen in buildings near the airport.
The streets of Kinshasa were crowded as his motorcade swept to the airport, with many residents coming out to watch and openly ask if the man who has ruled Zaire for 32 years would ever return.

In a sign of the increasing tension, Air France diverted its scheduled flight from Kinshasa to Congo, on the opposite side of the Zaire river. An airline official said the plane normally stays nine hours on the ground in Kinshasa, too long under current circumstances.
Mobutu, battling cancer and rebel advances, is to meet the presidents of Cameroon, Central African Republic, Chad, Congo, Equatorial Guinea and Gabon in Libreville, said a government statement.

The talks were described as a follow-up to a weekend peace summit between Mobutu, Kabila and South Africa's Nelson Mandela on a South African ship in the Congolese port of Pointe Noire. That meeting proved inconclusive.

But with Laurent Kabila's rebels saying they have the teeming city in their sights, newspapers in the city and ordinary Zaireans speculated that Mobutu, 66, would take advantage of the meeting to slip quietly into exile.
